A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe the same CIA Suite, HERCULE evaluator, and RECON benchmark. Text, tables, figures, and appendices A–G can be matched reliably; appendix pages 16–32 are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, comparisons with human judgments, and ablation experiments in Tables 1–7, with additional qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, human-evaluation, ablation, and qualitative results, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same Llama-3.1-8B-I fine-tuning procedure, English references and rubrics, target-language prompts and responses, and English feedback with 1–5 scores. No algorithm, architecture, or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same INTEL training data and RECON tasks across Bengali, German, French, Hindi, Telugu, and Urdu. The in-the-wild evaluation and cross-language transfer scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Llama-3.1-405B-I, Gemma, Aya23, Llama-3.2, and Sarvam. The joint-training, linear-merging, and TIES comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Both retain 100k training and 1k validation examples per language, the 4096-token limit, three training epochs, and the same evaluation metrics. The 100-prompt-per-language human-evaluation sampling and scoring procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 retains the same language-transfer, reference-answer, modeling-choice, and merging analyses. Tokenizer analysis, error cases, and merging examples in appendices B, F, and G are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The three-annotator averaging and inter-annotator agreement reporting also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain the same numerical entries. For example, Table 1 reports average kappa of 0.73 for HERCULE FFT and 0.64 for GPT-4o in both versions. Plotted findings and appendix qualitative examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The dataset tuple and generation/evaluation mappings in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning CIA, English-reference cross-lingual evaluation, alignment with human judgments, and transfer to unseen languages.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of evaluator generosity, reference neglect, tokenizer difficulties, and low-resource performance. Limitations concerning language coverage, available models, and unexplored merging configurations are unchanged.

D1.justification: AdamW, the 1e-5 learning rate, FlashAttention 2, eight H100 GPUs, and appendix prompt templates are unchanged. Code/data/model links and the release and licensing statements also remain the same.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are retained. Positioning relative to reference-based evaluators, multilingual evaluation, and model merging is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes Dilip Venkatesh’s affiliation from AI4Bharat to New York University, adjusts affiliation superscripts, and adds “Work done while at AI4Bharat.” Body wording and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised author block produces layout reflow. Table 5 moves from page 7 to page 8, Table 6 moves between columns on page 8, and the conclusion continues onto page 9. Figure and table content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 updates author information and reflows existing material. Methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices. These administrative and layout edits do not materially improve or weaken the paper’s overall quality.
